summary.text: Nily Rozic is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 25 in eastern Queens, first elected in 2012.

Born in Jerusalem and raised in Queens, she was chief of staff to Assemblymember Brian Kavanagh before her election. She chairs the Assembly Consumer Affairs and Protection Committee and is running unopposed for re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Rozic was born in Jerusalem and raised in Queens, according to her official Assembly biography. She graduated from New York University and from Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs, and NYU honored her with a Distinguished Young Alumni Award in 2022.
Before her own election she worked as Chief of Staff to Assemblymember Brian Kavanagh and served as a member of Community Board 8 and of the Townsend Harris High School Alumni Association.

Elected to the Assembly in 2012, Rozic became the youngest woman in the state legislature and the first woman to represent the 25th District, according to her official biography. The district includes Flushing, Fresh Meadows, Bayside, Douglaston and other eastern Queens communities.

She currently chairs the Committee on Consumer Affairs and Protection and sits on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees. She previously chaired the Subcommittee on Emerging Workforce, the Task Force on Women's Issues (2017) and the Office on State-Federal Relations (2020).
According to her official biography, she has sponsored legislation on workplace flexibility, fair work shifts and pay equity, and authored a law easing work schedules for state employees.

City & State named Rozic to its 2013 list of the Next Generation of Political Leaders, and The Jewish Week included her in its 36 Under 36. She took part in the Lindsay Fellowship Program's inaugural class (2017) at CUNY's Institute for Local and State Governance, and she lives in Fresh Meadows, according to her official biography.
